analysis:
Examined two files.

1) ProviderLoop+SSEParser.swift: the tool-call element type changed from OpenAIToolCall to OpenAIToolCallDelta in StreamChunkExtract (line 35), parseStreamChunk (line 127) and encodeToolCallsForHash (line 307). The hash encoding is unchanged: one \u{1F}tool_call:<JSON>\u{1F} marker per element, with sorted keys. Streamed fragments now each produce a marker in wire order, as the comment at lines 301-302 says. This changes the response-hash domain only for incremental tool calls, so the hash commits to the same bytes returned to the consumer. It does not weaken the commitment. The parser does not touch encryption, key handling or plaintext routing (T-008). The encoding-failure sentinel (line 317) is preserved. Open question: whether the downstream consumer of the hash and the coordinator or consumer reassembly treat fragment-wise markers consistently. That code is outside the supplied evidence, and the hash is a provider-reported integrity aid (T-007), not a trust anchor.

2) LaunchAgent.swift: two new keys, ToolStreamPreparation.streamToolCallsEnvironmentKey and ReasoningPromptProbe.plainTailContentSeedEnvironmentKey, are added to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (lines 296-297). They are persisted into the launchd plist EnvironmentVariables via passthroughEnvironment, which forwards only non-empty allowlisted values. These are behavior toggles with exact 0 as rollback. They do not touch the App Attest worker flag, native fault flags or the cache kill switch. The plist is user-owned. A local operator already controls the environment (ADV-001, TB-003), and no new privilege boundary is crossed. The definitions of the two key constants are not supplied, so I assume they are benign string constants.

No regression identified against T-041, T-053 or the TB-011 attestation controls. Nothing new in the cache or attestation surface.
